policy_metadata.policy_title: Long-Acting Reversible Contraception While Inpatient Postpartum

sections.heading: Overview
content: This policy outlines Humana’s reimbursement for long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) provided to a postpartum inpatient. LARC devices are a type of birth control that provides long-term pregnancy prevention. They are the most effective form of reversible birth control, with a failure rate of less than one percent. There are two types of LARC devices: intrauterine devices (IUDs) and implants.

sections.heading: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to only facility services. As used in this policy, x represents any appropriate frequency code, which is the final digit of the type of bill (TOB) code. Humana reimburses for a LARC device inserted for a postpartum inpatient separately from the inpatient hospital labor and delivery Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) payment. In such circumstances, insertion of the LARC device is reimbursed at the fee schedule rate. To facilitate such payment, the facility should submit a UB-04 claim form or its electronic equivalent with TOB 11x. The facility should report insertion of the LARC device with HCPCS codes J7296, J7297 , J7298 , J7300 , J7301 or J7307 . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, claims are subject to the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky out-of-network payment policy. For more information, see the relevant guidance in the References section of this policy.
